segments: The eighth series.
The Kings of the Romans.
especially in Egypt.
They were Caesars for fifteen years.
They persecuted the Christians.
And Shapur, the son of Ardashir, king of the Persians, devastated Syria, Cilicia, and Cappadocia.
And the Goths, when they crossed the river of Maebianos (of Maebios) (of Danubios?):
carried off the multitude of the eparchies into captivity.
And when Valerian was taken captive to Persia,
Gallienus gave rest to the Christians.
two years.
And at that time the Bruchion in Alexandria was destroyed.
And while pressed hard in battle, Claudius died in Sirmium.
And also the likeness of a crown was seen in the heavens.
afterwards, and subjugated the Gauls.
And in his time Mani became known.
And he gave his daughter to Shapur and made peace with him.
And Shapur built for himself a city in Persia resembling Constantinople, which is named Gandisabor (Gundishapur?):
and he settled his Roman wife in it.
And there came with her skilled men from among the Greek physicians,
and they sowed Hippocratic medicine in the East.
And there were also eminent Syrian {OCR?} physicians,
like Sergius of Resh'aina,
who was the first to translate philosophical and medical books from Greek into Syriac {OCR?};
and Athanasius of Amida,
and Philagrius,
and Simeon the Monk, who is known as 'of His Grace',
and Gregory the Bishop,
and Theodosius the Patriarch,
and the excellent Hunayn bar Ishaq,
and many others after them down to our own day,
all of them Syrians {OCR?}.
Now Aaron the Priest was not a Syrian {OCR?},
but a certain Giosios {Gesius} of Alexandria translated his book from Greek into Syriac {OCR?}.
And that Aurelian Caesar built a wall for Rome.
And while he was persecuting the Christians, he was swallowed by lightning and died. [variant footnote] six months.
And he was killed in Pontus.
And at this time there reigned in Persia [variant footnote] two months:
Hormizd.
